transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-25
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Mateo Singh (Redwood SE), Samira Holt (CSM) / Lena Ortiz (Head of ML), Raj Patel (Infra Lead), Marta Gomez (Security)

Auto-summary: (auto) CrestPoint is evaluating dedicated reserved GPUs to handle low-latency model scoring for their search/rerank pipeline. They need strong tenant isolation, predictable tail latency, and an economical burst strategy — potentially mixing warm pools + hosted fallback.

[00:00] Avery (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros?
[00:12] Lena (CrestPoint): yeah hi, lena here. we run a live rerank for search and a few realtime personalization endpoints. 1 to 5ms token latencies would be ideal but our current infra is spiky during batches.
[00:25] Raj (CrestPoint): infra lead, raj — we're trying to avoid spinning up huge fleet. want reserved GPUs but need isolation so one noisy tenant doesn't blow our P95.
[00:35] Mateo (Redwood SE): thanks, that makes sense. quick Q — are you leaning Hosted, Dedicated, or Private? or mixing?
[00:44] Lena: primary goal Dedicated reserved for production scoring. maybe Private later for regulated datasets. but Hosted as a fallback for big bursts — cost is a concern.
[00:55] Avery: great. we'll cover reserved sizing, warm-pools/prewarm, eviction tolerances, and fallback paths to hosted variants.

[01:15] Mateo: can you share your current qps and payloads? even rough percentiles help size reserved capacity — eg p50/p95/p99.
[01:24] Raj: sure, p50 is ~180 qps across 6 mids, p95 ~620 qps, p99 spikes to 1.2k for 90s windows. payloads avg 1.8k tokens in text input.
[01:40] Mateo: ok that drives GPU selection and slot counts. for those spikes we recommend a warm-pool of ephemeral nodes sized to absorb 30-40% of p95 burst with prewarm time of ~90-120s depending on model (kv cache warm).
[01:55] Lena: when you say "kv cache warm" do you mean model state warmup? how expensive is it?
[02:03] Mateo: yes, the KV cache and attention layers, plus any tokenizer instantiation. For large decoder models, cold-start can add 1.5–3s if you don't prewarm. with warm-pool and prefix caching you can get cold-starts down to ~200–400ms for shorter contexts, but depends on sequence length.

[02:30] Marta (Security): on isolation — we need tenant fencing, audit logs, and KMS integration. can Redwood guarantee no co-mingling of inference data in logs?
[02:40] Samira (CSM): we have dedicated pools that are tenant-isolated; logs can be routed to your account's storage, and we support envelope encryption with customer-managed KMS/HSM integration for Private. we'll share SOC2/ISO snippets.
[02:55] Marta: and SSO? we need SAML for console access and RBAC for operators.
[03:03] Avery: yes, SAML/SSO and SSO provisioning are supported, role-based access is configurable per pool. we'll include our security pack.

[03:25] Raj: eviction tolerances — what happens if the reserved pool fills and we have additional burst? preemption?
[03:32] Mateo: by policy you set a prewarm ratio and an eviction tolerance. if pool is full we have three levers: 1) queue requests up to a small latency budget, 2) fallback to a hosted lower-cost variant of the model (model variant with smaller context or quantized weights), or 3) call out to a separate burst pool (if reserved capacity purchased for bursts). Preemption is configurable — you can allow low-priority jobs to be evicted.
[03:58] Lena: fallback to quantized hosted variant — what's the expected delta in output quality?
[04:06] Mateo: varies. in our internal benchmarks quantized variants typically have small degradation on rerank tasks (up to 2–4% quality drop) but huge cost/latency win. we can run evals on your prompt set in the pilot.

[04:30] (brief cross-talk)
[04:42] Raj: pricing question — do you charge for warm-pool idle nodes? how is burst billed?
[04:50] Avery: reserved capacity has a flat monthly commit for the baseline capacity. warm-pool idle nodes are priced lower than full reserved nodes if kept as "standby"; burst beyond reserved is billed usage-based (per-token / per-second) when using Hosted fallback or on-demand nodes. we'll include a detailed cost model.

[05:15] Lena: regulatory note: for PHI-adjacent data we might need Private deployment later. is the Private control plane fully separated?
[05:25] Samira: Private gives you a separate control plane and optional air-gapped on-prem packaging. KMS can be customer-managed. we'll outline the migration path in the docs.

[06:00] Mateo: another sizing note — sequence length distribution matters a lot. if you have long queries frequently, we recommend extra headroom on reserved GPUs. can you share distribution?
[06:10] Raj: 70% short (<256 tokens), 25% medium (256–1024), 5% long (>1024).
[06:20] Mateo: ok that helps, warm-pool prewarm time for long queries is higher; we can recommend mixed node types and a hot lane for short queries.

[07:00] Marta: audit logs — do you preserve request payloads? we need redaction options.
[07:08] Samira: yes, request logging is configurable; you can redact personal data at the edge, and we keep metadata only if you choose. will include the logging options.

[08:00] (discussion about canary rollouts)
[08:15] Avery: for rollouts we support canary traffic routing and A/B by route/model version with automatic fallback to previous version on regressions.
[08:30] Lena: good, we need a canary that cuts over in 5% increments and auto-fails back on latency or quality regressions.
[08:40] Mateo: we can wire that up in the pilot and hook your eval set to monitor regressions in near real-time.

[09:10] Raj: concrete ask — we want a 3-month pilot to validate warm-pool sizing, economics, and tail latency under realistic load.
[09:18] Avery: pilot plan: 2-week ingest of metrics and load patterns, then a 1-week stress window, plus continuous evals. Mateo will run the benchmark harness and collect P50/P95/P99, token costs, and failover stats.

[09:45] (interruptions, brief small talk)
[10:05] Mateo: one more technical piece — KV cache sharing: we do per-tenant KV cache on dedicated pools, but note that large batch warm-ups can evict micro-caches. you can configure sticky sessions for high-priority flows.
[10:25] Raj: sticky sessions sound helpful for our personalization endpoint. how do you handle cross-tenant blast radius?
[10:33] Mateo: tenant fencing + cgroup isolation + scheduler limits. in Private or Dedicated fully dedicated pools you get stronger isolation. we'll provide an ops playbook.

[11:10] Marta: compliance flow — will you sign a DPA and provide subprocessor list?
[11:18] Samira: yes to DPA; we'll share the subprocessor list and SOC2 inc summary.

[11:40] Lena: timeline — we're aiming to move scoring in 3 months, pilot next month. any blockers?
[11:48] Avery: no blockers from Redwood once we get your traffic percentiles and sign simple pilot NDA/contract. pricing approvals on your side could shift timeline.

[12:05] (recap)
[12:12] Avery: quick recap: 1) we'll send pricing + burst model, 2) security pack and DPA, 3) Mateo will prepare benchmark harness, 4) CrestPoint to share traffic percentiles + sample payloads. pilot scheduling for early September.
[12:30] Lena: perfect. please add an item for a short 30-min tech kickoff before the benchmark.
[12:38] Avery: noted, we'll schedule.

[12:50] (end)

Post-meeting notes: agreed pilot scope and artifacts to be exchanged. Customer expressed sensitivity about eviction behavior and wants a tight fallback that preserves quality. They mentioned Anthropic as a competitive option they're evaluating for hosted fallback, and they compare in-house cost vs Redwood's committed pricing.
